## Strategy

The rules work from sensors alone, so they hold on any grid size, goal placement or patrol cycle.

1. **Make progress.** Prefer moves that reduce the distance to the next unreached goal (`toward`). Since every such move shrinks the distance, the agent cannot circle forever while it has safe progress moves.
2. **Stay safe.** Never take a move whose target is on the patrol path (`patrol`), on a goal that must not be entered yet (`early`), or where the obstacle will be right after the move (`obstacle`). Also avoid moves whose slip could land on the patrol or an early goal (`risky`).
3. **Fall back gracefully.** If no safe progress move exists, take a safe sideways or wall-bumping move. The obstacle's phase changes every step, so waiting is only safe when it ends, and the fallback lets the phase advance. Each fallback level drops one requirement, from "no risky slip" to "any non-collision move".
4. **Last resort.** The final `true` rule covers states where every action is unsafe. It is needed to end the list, but the adversary can pick any action there.

Because the first rule with `any` only applies when at least one action qualifies, it only offers moves that are both safe and progressing. The fallbacks are ordered so that the stricter safety conditions take precedence over the looser ones.

```json
  {"condition": "toward & !wall & !patrol & !early & !risky & !obstacle", "action": "any"},
  {"condition": "!wall & !patrol & !early & !risky & !obstacle", "action": "any"},
  {"condition": "!wall & !patrol & !early & !obstacle", "action": "any"},
  {"condition": "!patrol & !early & !obstacle", "action": "any"},
  {"condition": "true", "action": "any"}
]}
```
